reasons.A: Short, declarative sentences in the present tense that relay the man's views in free indirect speech, a dry ironic stance and a closing aphorism that turns on the reader match the passage's movement and wit most closely; only slightly heavier with flourishes.
reasons.C: Period diction and the measured, gently ironic reporting ('I ventured to suggest', 'would have done credit to a deacon') fit well, but the sentences run more evenly and the close explains rather than lands a generalising turn.
reasons.B: Modern, plain register and an earnest psychological close ('That was the unsettling part', 'pointed in the wrong direction') lack the passage's Latinate diction, dry irony and aphoristic generalisations.
